A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that there are many factors that influence the development of surgical site infections (SSIs) and that the surgeon is not one of them.
the incidence of wound infection in the first 48 h is 2 per cent, in 48–72 h 1 per cent and after 72 h 2 per cent.
we have shown that a single dose of antibiotic at the induction of anaesthesia does not reduce the risk of surgical site infections (SSI).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the incidence of postoperative infection is not related to the type of mesh, the method of fixation or the method of wound closure.
the risk of infection is not a major deterrent to the use of mesh in hernia repairs and is probably overemphasized by the public and the medical community.
the incidence of wound infection after elective surgery in the United Kingdom is much higher than previously thought.
